Hence the greedy scan accepts $x$, proving $S\in\mathcal F$.", "note": "Self-duality (1) plus (2) gives the membership characterization for all m >= a_1."}, "L6.2": {"established": "yes", "quote": "Let $P$ be the union of all terminal members. It is a finite set of primes. If a prime $p$ occurs in any $C\in\mathcal C$, Lemma 2 supplies a terminal $D\in\mathcal C$ containing $p$. Therefore every prime occurring in any member of $\mathcal C$ belongs to $P$.", "note": "Different route (sunflower Lemma 1 + weight descent Lemma 2) but proves finiteness of relevant primes for all terms."}, "L6.3": {"established": "yes", "quote": "Taking $x=a_n$ and using (6), the endpoint $a_n+L$ is accepted. It is consequently the $T$-th accepted integer after $a_n$, so
\[
a_{n+T}=a_n+L
\]
for every positive integer $n$.", "note": "Periodicity valid from n=1; membership invariance mod L proved for all m >= a_1."}}, "S_ref": 2, "notes": "Complete alternative proof: self-duality of accepted supports, sunflower argument bounding minimal supports of bounded size, and an arithmetic weight descent using a_1 to force every prime into a finite terminal set. Checked each step; no reliance on mere pairwise intersection, and periodicity holds from n=1."}
